topics.topic: Atomicity, durable state, and retry cleanup when spool removal and run ending or release only partially succeed
questions: If removing the spool fails after the run-ending or release record is written, is that record retained, is the transition refused or rolled back, and when and by whom is the leftover spool removed?
If recording `released_by`/`released_at` succeeds but removing the spool fails, or removal succeeds but recording fails, what durable state and retry behavior must result?

quotes:
Every record is written through `module:store`, one call and one transaction
(K-17).

A step that says "writes" means one such store call by the module
named; a store call that fails changes no record (A18 rules 3-4) and the request
is answered as an internal error by `module:surface` (A16 rule 7).

`surface` owns it: every failure it
answers `internal_error` — a store failure, an unconfirmed cleanup, any
unexpected exception — is answered first, and then `surface.serve_kernel`
ends the process with a non-zero status, so the next start derives every
run (A14 rules 5 and 7).

`capability:runs.release_run` refuses a run that is not
   `failed` or was already released; otherwise it records who and when, and
   `capability:store.remove_run_spool` removes the run's files (A14 rule 4).

`capability:runs.recover_running_runs`: first names to
   `capability:store.remove_run_spool` every ended run that does not keep its
   spool (A14 rule 4, A18 rule 4); then derives every run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval`
   or `pending` — from its records, oldest first, rewriting a lagging status
   or waiting point and reaching again, through
   `capability:effects.reach_operation_element`, an operation element whose
   wait no longer holds (A14 rule 5); then, as the kernel actor, advances every
   run left `running`, oldest first: a function element without a concluded
   record is executed again; a `read` element without one is sent again; an
   operation element of another class with neither a concluded record nor an
   EffectAttempt is reached as for the first time, an unused approval covering
   it only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A14 rule 5).

Spools of ended runs that keep none are removed, except one that cannot be
  removed, which stays until a later start removes it; spools of `failed`
  unreleased runs stay.
judgement.why: The release or ending record is written before removal, a later removal failure cannot roll back that completed transaction, the kernel stops after the internal error, and startup retries removal; removal cannot succeed before a failed release record because the specified order records first.

topics.topic: How a read is resent after service_unreachable without authority
questions: Does the `otherwise` include a `read` element, contradicting A11 rule 1 that a read needs no authority, or is a read resent without an approval or grant?

topics.topic: How draft-write sends are represented when authorized by flow activation
questions: How is a normal `draft-write` send represented in this outcome, since the accepted rules say it is sent under the flow activation without an approval preview or a grant?

topics.topic: How recovery durably prevents repeated execution when recording cleanup failure also fails
questions: If writing the `cleanup_failed` NodeExecution itself fails, may the next start execute the same element again and encounter the cleanup failure repeatedly, or is some additional durable mechanism required to uphold the stated no-loop guarantee?

topics.topic: How runs resolves and validates an effect-owned approval or attempt to its run and element
questions: How does `module:runs` obtain and validate the run and element belonging to an `approval_id` before `module:effects` changes the approval, given that no capability reads an approval or resolves it to its run?
How does `module:runs` identify and validate the run and element belonging to the named EffectAttempt before `module:effects` resolves it, when no EffectAttempt read or lookup capability is offered?

topics.topic: Whether kernel startup mutations are transactional or may remain after startup failure
questions: Does “no partial start” mean only that the MCP surface remains closed, while earlier cleanup and recovery writes remain committed if a later startup step fails, or must all startup mutations be rolled back?

topics.topic: Which contract version governs activation of an admitted implementation
questions: When an admitted implementation belongs to an older, non-current contract version of the slot, does submission inspect and activate that implementation's contract version, inspect the slot's current contract version, or refuse the submission?

topics.topic: Which module owns refusal of start_run for an unknown flow
questions: Which module owns the unknown-reference refusal when `start_run` names a flow that does not exist: `flows`, which owns the Flow record, or `runs`, which owns the start checks?
